summary: Red team of the area Étale cohomology (Algebraic geometry): AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons, ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology, DeligneWeightsAndPurity, EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves, HabiroCohomologyFoundations, LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles, WeightsInEtaleCohomology and WeilConjectures. That is 76 stages, the 61 paper routes into them and their Part IIs, and the eleven restructuring proposals that touch them. 40 findings: 6 high, 30 medium, 4 low. High: (1) Deligne's equidistribution theorem and Katz–Sarnak monodromy of the universal curve are planned nowhere, although an accepted route sends Schiffmann's density theorem, which needs both, into DWP.0. (2) Gabber's absolute purity is planned twice, by accepted routes into SF.2 and into a new Part II. (3) No layer plans ℓ-adic sheaf theory on Artin or DM stacks, which shtuka, Hitchin and Bun_G consumers apply EDC's outputs to. (4) de Jong's alterations in L5 need M̄_{g,n} with a projective cover, which nothing plans. (5) Huber 3.8.1 in characteristic p (H5) needs relative Poincaré duality in all dimensions, while H3 plans only curves. (6) HQ.5's Theorem 4.22 lacks both proof inputs. Medium findings include: the uniform Lang–Weil estimate and Ekedahl's Chebotarev are unowned; routes still point at owners that accepted RS-17 reassigned; the Artin–Schreier sheaf is planned three times; the IndConstructibles Part II re-plans Mathlib's Serre-class localization; missing edges L3 → EDC.6, SF.2 → L1, HR.1 → HQ.1 and HQ.5-trace → HQ.7; de Jong alterations and coherent Grothendieck duality each have two owners; characteristic-0 characteristic cycles have no accepted owner; LPV.2's algebraic Picard–Lefschetz proof lacks its source (Illusie 2002); the shared Part II ids lose one paper's brief in make_queue.py; and the Habiro family's q-de Rham–Witt theory is planned twice pending the accepted PLAN-HABIRO.

findings.where: PAPER-SCHIFFMANN-16 route 3 (accepted) → DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.0, item PAPER-SCHIFFMANN-16/36; Weil II §3.5
findings.claim: An accepted source route sends Schiffmann's Proposition 4.8 (the Weil numbers of genus-g curves are Zariski dense in T_g/W_g) into DWP.0, which only defines Weil q-numbers and cannot prove it. Its proof (Appendix B) needs two things no layer plans and the libraries lack: the Katz–Sarnak theorem that the geometric monodromy of R¹ρ_!Q_ℓ over an open of M_g has Zariski closure Sp_2g, and Deligne's equidistribution theorem (Weil II 3.5.3). Weil II §3.5 falls between DWP.8 (§3.4) and LPV.7:invariant-cycles (§3.6) and is in no stage's sources.
findings.evidence: DWP.0 (data/atlas.json): 'Sources: Weil I §§1.4–1.7/3.1; Weil II §§1.2/1.6; no general weight theorem', requiring only EDC.0. Route 3 reason: 'The statement proved in this paper's Appendix B is of the same kind'; review: 'accept … the purity/weight statement about Frobenius eigenvalues'. Schiffmann arXiv:1406.3839v2, Appendix B: 'By [KS, Thm 10.1.16, Thm. 10.2.2], the Zariski closure of ρ(π1^geom(M°_g)) is equal to Sp(2g, Ql)… By Deligne's equidistribution theorem (see [D1, 3.5.3] and [KS, Thm. 9.2.6]) …'. Weil II table of contents: '(3.5) Application : théorèmes d'équidistribution … 210'. Stage sources: DWP.7 '3.3.1–3.3.11', DWP.8 '3.4.1–3.4.13', LPV.7:invariant-cycles 'Deligne II 3.6.1'. A search of all stage descriptions finds no stage in DWP, LPV, EDC, WIC or WC mentioning equidistribution, and none mentioning Katz–Sarnak.
findings.fix: Add a DWP layer (e.g. DWP.8:equidistribution, requiring DWP.5, DWP.7, DWP.8) owning Weil II 3.5.1–3.5.3, with the function-field Sato–Tate statements 3.5.5–3.5.7 as acceptance and Haar probability imported from tauceti RepresentationTheory/CompactGroups. Extend the accepted Part II 'LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles, Part II: universal hypersurface monodromy' (BROWNING-SAWIN-20 route 6, which owns Katz–Sarnak 11.4.9) with Katz–Sarnak 10.1.16/10.2.2 for the universal curve. Re-route SCHIFFMANN-16/36 to the new DWP layer; DWP.0 keeps only the Weil-number bookkeeping. Record Schiffmann's [D1] label ('La conjecture de Weil I', but 'Publ. Math. 52' = Weil II) as a source issue.

findings.where: AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L5 task 2 (node L5/de-jong-5-8-curve-fibration-alteration)

L5 task 2: 'Consume a proved stable-curve supplier where its hypotheses agree; otherwise the needed curve-family theorem is a task of this stage'; its decomposition gap lists §§5.11–5.13 ('the citation of Deligne-Mumford/Knudsen') as unread. findings.where: ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H5 (Huber 3.8.1 in characteristic p) and H3
findings.claim: ECD 27.2 applies Huber's Theorem 3.8.1 over a characteristic-p field to affine m-space for every m, and H5 owns that case. Huber's recorded proof in characteristic p (Berkovich's comparison) needs relative Poincaré duality for smooth morphisms of every dimension. H5's only duality supplier, H3, plans duality for curves only ('Poincaré duality for curves'), and the Zavyalov route adds only the absolute smooth proper case. So H5's proof has an unplanned input.
findings.evidence: ECD p. 164: '… by … [Hub96, Theorem 3.8.1] … RΓ(X_C,A) → RΓ(X_C^◇, c*A) is an isomorphism' for C the completed algebraic closure of F̄p((t)). Decomposition node H5/comparison-over-nonarchimedean-fields-3-8-1: 'if char k > 0, as Berkovich's comparison [Ber1, 7.5], using cohomology with proper support … (5.7.2) and Poincaré duality (7.5.3)'. Berkovich 1993, Lemma 7.5.2 (printed p. 147): 'φ is smooth of pure dimension d … R^qφ_*(F) ≅ (R^{2d−q}φ_!(F^∨))^∨(−d)'. H3 title 'Proper support, traces and Poincaré duality for curves'; text: 'For smooth analytic curves … construct the trace and the duality pairing'. ZAVYALOV-25/2 (→ H3) is 'smooth proper … H^i ⊗ H^{2d−i} → F_ℓ perfect'.
findings.fix: Add a suffix H3:smooth-duality with Huber 5.7.2, 7.2.2 and 7.5.3 for smooth morphisms of pure dimension d, all d (sources Berkovich 7.2.1, 7.3.1, 7.4.9, transported by the Huber–Berkovich comparison, ZAVYALOV-25/136–139), keep the curve part as the early prefix that S4/S5 consume, and add the edge H3:smooth-duality → H5.

findings.evidence: QW.6: 'γ_i of R[[q−1]] that lift T_j↦q^{δij}T_j … q-∂_i f=(γ_i f−f)/(qT_i−T_i) … twisted Leibniz rule … q-Ω*_{R/A,□} is the Koszul complex … q-Ω/(q−1)≅Ω'. QWittVectors boundary: 'Its p-complete framed complexes over ℤ_p[[q−1]] are the completed base changes of QW.6's framed complexes for A=ℤ; PR.6 builds them without importing QW'. PR.6: 'framed polynomial computation, change of framing and cocycle descent … the p-completed framed q-de Rham complex'. HQ.1: 'Import … framed q-difference complex … from PrismaticCohomology PR.6'.
findings.fix: Record one owner for framed q-derivatives and the framed q-de Rham/q-Hodge Koszul complexes in the general form over an I-completely étale framing (I = (q−1) or (p, q−1)): split QW.6's framing prefix into a stage not needing QW.5 and have PR.6 import and p-complete it; PR.6 keeps q-PD envelopes (BS22 Lemma 16.21), the q-crystalline site and the prismatic comparison; HQ.1 imports from the single owner.

findings.where: HabiroCohomologyFoundations:HQ.3
findings.claim: HQ.3 puts Wagner v2 Theorem 3.11(b) on the wrong object. The atlas says the ascending filtration with gr ≃ Σ^{−i} q-W_m dR^i lives on qHdg/(q^m−1), with qHdg the (q−1)-completed colimit; in the source it lives on q-𝓗dg/(q^m−1), the Habiro–Hodge complex. On the (q−1)-complete object only (q−1)-completed graded pieces are obtained, so for m > 1 the statement as written is false.
findings.evidence: Wagner arXiv:2510.04782v2 p. 25 (rendered): '(b) For all m ∈ ℕ, the quotient q-𝓗dg_{−/A}/(q^m−1) admits an exhaustive ascending filtration'; p. 6: for the (q−1)-complete version 'H*(q-Hdg_{S/ℤ,□}/(q^m−1)) ≅ (q-W_mΩ*)^∧_(q−1)'; p. 7: the result 'holds true, even without the (q−1)-completion'. HQ.3's text places the filtration on the (q−1)-completed colimit.
findings.fix: Rewrite HQ.3: construct q-𝓗dg_{R/A} = lim_m q-𝓗dg_{R/A,m} (from 3.42–3.45) and put the filtration on q-𝓗dg_{R/A}/(q^m−1); state that for the (q−1)-complete qHdg only the (q−1)-completed version holds.
